blind_spots: The supplied dates extend into 2026 and were not independently verified.
The Reddit and several social posts provide titles or unrelated statements but no usable findings about quality-control pain points.
Much of the workflow evidence comes from commercial vendor blogs, limiting independent validation.
There are no longitudinal comparisons, failure-rate metrics, or quantified estimates of how much human QA is required.
No substantive evidence measures character, visual, voice, or brand consistency across multiple installments of a series.
The evidence contains little direct creator testimony about reproducing a specific personal quality bar or house style.
contradictions: The claim that AI output requires knowledgeable review is qualified by niche evidence that a set-it-and-forget-it email capability was considered a major time-saver for small businesses.
Version confusion is not universal: the G2 evidence says real-time co-editing and inline collaboration can eliminate version confusion and slow email chains.
The evidence credits AI tools with time-saving batch processing and broad editing options even while reporting that they can lack professional depth and be unintuitive.
